text: Employing a within-subject design, West and colleagues (246) recruited 12 untrained men to perform elbow flexion exercise on separate days under two hormonal conditions: a low-hormone condition in which one arm performed elbow flexion exercise only and a high-hormone condition in which the contralateral arm performed the same arm curl exercise followed immediately by multiple sets of lower-body resistance training designed to promote a robust systemic response. After 15 weeks, increases in muscle cross-sectional area were similar between conditions despite significantly higher post-exercise concentrations of circulating IGF-1, GH, and testosterone in those in the high-hormone condition.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 1: Hypertrophy-Related Responses and Adaptations to Exercise Stress
